 2          1.      I am a member of the bar of the State of California and an attorney at Quinn Emanuel

 3 Urquhart & Sullivan, LLP, attorneys for Defendant World Liberty Financial LLC (“World Liberty”)

 7 Dkt. No. 3.

 9 Another Party’s Material Should be Sealed. Dkt. No. 3. I have reviewed the Complaint that

10 Plaintiffs seek to file under seal pursuant to Civil Local Rule 79-5(f), an unredacted version of which

11 has been filed at Dkt. No. 3.

12          4.      Courts generally apply a compelling reasons standard when considering motions to

13 seal documents. Kamakana v. City and Cnty. of Honolulu, 447 F.3d 1172, 1178 (9th Cir. 2006).

14          5.      Based on my review, there are compelling reasons to seal the highlighted portions of

15 the Complaint, which includes World Liberty’s sensitive business information and quotes directly

16 from an agreement with broad confidentiality provisions.

17          6.      The Complaint contains confidential, sensitive business information of World

18 Liberty. The public disclosure of World Liberty’s confidential, sensitive business information poses

19 significant risks to World Liberty’s commercial and competitive standing, including allowing

20 competitors to gain insight into World Liberty’s contractual practices, preferences, and strategy.
21 Disclosing this information will also harm World Liberty’s leverage in future negotiations with

22 business partners and investors.

23          7.      In order to prevent potential harm to World Liberty, Defendant respectfully requests
24 that the Court keep the highlighted portions of Plaintiffs’ Complaint under seal. See e.g., In re Elec.

25 Arts, Inc., 298 F. App’x 568, 569 (9th Cir. 2008) (“[T]he U.S. Supreme Court established that . . .

26 ‘the common-law right of inspection has bowed before the power of a court to insure that its records

27 are not used … as sources of business information that might harm a litigant’s competitive

28 standing.’” (quoting Nixon v. Warner Commc’ns, Inc., 435 U.S. 589, 598 (1978))); Jam Cellars,

 4 purpose, and subject matters of the confidential agreement entered into between the parties. That

 5 confidential agreement itself defines these terms as confidential information and prohibits parties
 6 from disclosing them to any third party. See Jam Cellars, Inc., 2020 WL 5576346, at *1 (“Courts

 7 have found that ‘confidential business information’ in the form of ‘license agreements, financial

 8 terms, details of confidential licensing negotiations, and business strategies’ satisfies the

10 Liberty negotiated with Blue Anthem Limited and Black Anthem Limited, including the unlock

11 percentage, the consideration paid, and the transfer restriction enforcement mechanisms. Disclosure

12 to the public would give World Liberty’s counterparties a roadmap to demand identical or more

13 favorable terms, directly undermining World Liberty’s negotiating position. It would harm World

14 Liberty’s ongoing token sale negotiations, relationships with existing institutional investors who

15 negotiated similar terms under confidentiality, and its ability to enforce confidentiality obligations

16 against other counterparties.

18 contract terms, which constitute “the truly sensitive information in [the] document,” pursuant to

19 Civil Local Rule 79-5(a). There is no less restrictive alternative available than permitting this

20 limited information to be filed under seal.

 1          Pursuant to Local Rule 7-12, Plaintiffs Yuchen “Justin” Sun (“Mr. Sun”), Blue Anthem

 3   “Plaintiffs”), and Defendant World Liberty Financial LLC (f/k/a World Liberty Financial, Inc.)

 4   (“World Liberty”), by and through their respective counsel of record, stipulate as follows:

 5          WHEREAS, Plaintiffs have filed a Complaint in this action (the “Action”) asserting claims

 6   against World Liberty for breach of contract, fraud, conversion, unjust enrichment, breach of the

 7   implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing, and declaratory relief arising from disputes related

 8   to certain cryptographically secured digital $WLFI tokens, and World Liberty contends that these

 9   claims are meritless and subject to mandatory arbitration;

10          WHEREAS, World Liberty denies Plaintiffs’ allegations in the Action, including the

11   allegations set forth herein, and nothing in this Stipulation shall be construed as an admission of

12   liability, wrongdoing, or the validity of any of Plaintiffs’ claims by World Liberty;

13          WHEREAS, World Liberty contends that Mr. Sun is not a party to the underlying

14   agreements and World Liberty did not consent to jurisdiction of this Court for any claims brought

15   by Mr. Sun; and the dispute between Black Anthem, Blue Anthem, and World Liberty is subject to

16   mandatory arbitration, and that this dispute, if it is to be maintained, should proceed in arbitration

17   and cannot proceed in the United States District Court for the Northern District of California, or

18   any other public court;

19          WHEREAS, without admitting or conceding any of the claims or allegations in the Action,

20   or that this is an appropriate forum for this dispute, the parties wish to resolve the issue of

21   preservation of Plaintiffs’ $WLFI tokens (the “Tokens at Issue”) pending adjudication of this

22   Action without the need for contested motion practice;

24   undersigned counsel, subject to the approval of the Court, as follows:

25      1. World Liberty shall not burn, destroy, reallocate to a burn address, or otherwise permanently

26          dispose of any of the Tokens at Issue, in whole or in part.

28          https://governance.worldlibertyfinancial.com/t/proposal-early-supporter-founder-team-
